name: agent-tools
description: Cross-project tooling: plugins maintained here, plus vetted third-party writing skills referenced from their upstream repositories.

plugins.name: overleaf-tracked-changes
plugins.description: Read and edit Overleaf documents as real tracked changes from a terminal session, with no browser.

plugins.name: humanizer
plugins.description: Rewrites text to strip the patterns that mark it as machine-written, working from Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing". Two passes, plus an optional voice profile calibrated against your own earlier writing.

plugins.name: academic-humanizer
plugins.description: The same de-AI pass, but constrained so scholarly convention survives it: citations, data, and numbers are left untouched, and claims are held to the strength the evidence actually supports. Has an NSF/NIH proposal mode.

plugins.name: paper-writing-skill
plugins.description: A five-stage pipeline for research papers — brainstorm, architect, draft, integrate, compress — with per-section rhetorical moves, a style audit on every edit, and an independent red-team pass. Calibrated for systems and ML venues.

plugins.name: academic-writing-skills
plugins.description: Submission-time tooling for LaTeX manuscripts: drafting the cover letter and searching for citations. Pruned to the two skills nothing else here covers — upstream's prose polisher, submission audit, Chinese-thesis, and Typst skills are not loaded.
